votes.evidence:
Premise traced from the callers and confirmed, with one correction to severity.

Call path: `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-143` (`handle_task_run_saved`, a `post_save` on `TaskRun`) fires only when a save touches `output` and it carries `pr_url`; on `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` it schedules `_start_stamphog_review` (`receivers.py:210-234`), which calls the facade `queue_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-154`) = a bare `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)`, with every exception swallowed by `logger.exception` (`receivers.py:233-234`). Nothing is persisted before the Celery task.

The task: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109` declares `@shared_task(ignore_result=True, max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)`. Config-resolution failure (`:1148-1150`), generic GitHub fetch failure (`:1163-1165`) and run-creation/on_commit workflow-start failure (`:1235-1237`) all `raise ...retry(exc=e)` with the 5 s default, so a non-rate-limit outage is given ~15-20 s total before Celery raises `MaxRetriesExceededError` and drops the job. Only `GitHubRateLimitError` gets a >=60 s countdown (`:1161-1162`). For the fetch-failure and config-failure branches no `ReviewRun` row exists yet, so there is no persisted "failed" state to reconcile; for the post-commit start failure a `ReviewRun` stays `QUEUED` with no workflow (`:366-381` shows `_start_review_workflow` propagates everything except `WorkflowAlreadyStartedError`).

No reconciliation exists: the only beat surface in stamphog is the daily digest (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/schedules.py`, `tasks/digest.py`); nothing sweeps stranded QUEUED inbox runs or missed hand-offs.

Recovery paths are all incidental, as the finding says:
- Another `output` save carrying `pr_url`: `set_task_run_output` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2138-2154`) would re-fire the receiver, but the agent server only syncs metadata when the branch changes (receivers.py docstring `:28-30`), and the tasks webhook backstop `_record_run_output_field` is idempotent and returns early once `pr_url` is set (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:283-292`), so no later save is guaranteed.
- Webhook carve-out re-review only on `synchronize`/`reopened` or base retarget (`tasks.py:49`, `:144-170`); `ready_for_review` is deliberately excluded (`:161-163`), and a manual `labeled` trigger is blocked for this PR class by `_review_skip_reason` (draft at `:227-228`, bot author at `:229-231`). So neither flipping the draft to ready nor adding the review label can recover a lost initial review; only a new push can.

The author's own comment (`tasks.py:1152-1154`) acknowledges "the toggle-gated initial review has no webhook redelivery behind it" and chose retry-over-drop as the mitigation, but the chosen policy gives that retry a ~15 s window.
votes.refutation:
Attempted refutation: the policy is a direct copy of the existing webhook path. `process_pull_request_event` uses the identical `max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5` (`tasks.py:809`), and the webhook view ACKs 202 before the task runs (`products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:64`), so GitHub does not auto-redeliver either; the whole product already accepts a ~15 s retry window with only manual GitHub redelivery as fallback. That makes this consistent with precedent rather than a new class of defect, and the review's "must_fix" plus its suggestion of a persisted request + periodic reconciler are oversized for the gap.

Why the refutation does not fully hold: the webhook path at least has a human recovery lever (redeliver from GitHub's UI), whereas for this PR class every manual lever is closed (label trigger refused as draft/bot, ready_for_review excluded from the carve-out), so an outage longer than ~15 s during the hand-off silently loses the feature's primary trigger until an unrelated push. Blast radius is one missed draft-time verdict on a PR that is still babysat and re-reviewed on the next push, and each attempt is logged via `logger.exception`, so it is not user-facing data loss. Appropriate fix is small: longer/backoff retries (e.g. `retry_backoff=True`, higher `max_retries`, or a countdown floor like the rate-limit branch), not a reconciliation subsystem. Severity should_fix, not must_fix.

votes.evidence:
Mechanics of the claim hold, but the premises that make it must_fix do not.

What the code does (worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):
- products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109 declares `process_inbox_pr_review` with `max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5`; config/DB failures (1150), fetch failures (1162-1165) and run-creation/workflow-start failures (1237) all call `.retry(exc=e)`. Rate-limit retries back off `max(retry_after, 60)` (1162).
- Celery re-raises `exc` once `retries > max_retries` (.flox/cache/venv/.../celery/app/task.py:765-768); with `ignore_result=True` nothing is persisted, so an exhausted task leaves only a log line.
- The webhook carve-out only covers `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = {synchronize, reopened}` + base retarget (tasks.py:49, 168-169); the docstring at 160-161 says the initial review is the receiver leg's job only. No periodic reconciler exists: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/schedules.py has only the digest crontab, and posthog/tasks/scheduled.py:97,808 registers only that.

Why it is not must_fix:
- Precedent: the webhook path `process_pull_request_event` uses the identical policy `max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5` (tasks.py:809) and GitHub does not auto-redeliver failed webhooks either, so the "no redelivery fallback" contrast the finding draws does not exist; this is the product's accepted retry envelope, not a regression introduced here.
- The "may not save another output" premise is weaker than stated: the receiver refires on every TaskRun save touching `output` with a `pr_url` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:88-95, 126-141; tests test_inbox_trigger.py:169-190), and a normal run produces at least two such saves minutes apart: the pr_url stamp (`_record_run_pr_url`, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:196-212, or the agent-server output merge at products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2016) and the agent's final `set_task_run_output`, which explicitly preserves `pr_url` (facade/api.py:2148-2154). A later push also re-reviews via the carve-out.
- Existing guards cover the partial-failure cases: the head-keyed dedupe restarts a stranded QUEUED run and recreates after FAILED (tasks.py:1195-1215; test_tasks.py:967-1000 ids `stranded_queued_run_restarts`, `failed_run_recreated_on_refire`).
- Egress shedding cannot turn the blip into a long outage: `StamphogGitHubClient._request` sends with `Priority.CRITICAL` (products/stamphog/backend/logic/github_client.py:443), and shedding applies only to BATCH/NORMAL (posthog/egress/github/transport.py:29).

Residual real gap: an outage that spans both refires' ~15 s windows (a multi-minute Temporal/DB/GitHub outage) drops the initial review with no persisted, retryable state, and the run is never created or is left QUEUED with no sweeper. That is a hardening opportunity shared with the webhook path, not a defect specific to this diff.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: (1) looked for a periodic reconciler of QUEUED/absent runs - none (schedules.py, scheduled.py:808 only digest); (2) looked for the webhook path covering `opened` for inbox PRs - excluded by `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` (tasks.py:49, 168); (3) looked for Celery settings that extend retries - none (no acks_late/autoretry config in posthog/). What did land: the identical retry policy on the webhook path (tasks.py:809) shows this is the established envelope; the receiver's refire-on-every-output-save plus the head-keyed dedupe (tasks.py:1195-1215, tests at test_tasks.py:967-1000) give a normal run a second and third chance minutes apart; and `Priority.CRITICAL` (github_client.py:443) rules out egress shedding extending a "blip" into hours. So the failure needs a multi-minute outage spanning every refire, which is reachable but narrow. Downgraded from must_fix to consider.

votes.evidence:
Reachability in production configuration checked in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215:

1. Retry budget is ~15 s. `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109` declares `@shared_task(ignore_result=True, max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)`; every failure branch (config lookup :1141-1142, GitHub fetch :1155-1160, run create / post-commit workflow start :1235-1237) calls `.retry(exc=e)` with no backoff, so after 4 attempts spanning roughly 15 s (or ~60 s steps only for the rate-limit branch :1157) Celery re-raises the exception and the task is dropped. `posthog/settings/celery.py:33-36` enables eager mode only under `TEST`, so in prod this really runs on a worker with that budget.

2. No reconciliation exists. The only stamphog beat entry is the daily digest (`posthog/tasks/scheduled.py:97, :808`). Grep for QUEUED sweeps finds only the opportunistic in-task restarts (`tasks.py:386-410`, `:1197-1213`); nothing periodically finds an inbox PR whose initial run was never created.

3. Refire is not guaranteed. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:81-83` re-fires only on a TaskRun save that touches `output`. The only writers of `TaskRun.output` are `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2153-2154` (agent-server `set_output`, called when the agent chooses) and `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:283-292` (`_record_run_output_field`, which returns early once `pr_url` is already set, so it is one-shot). The other recovery path is a later push reaching stamphog's own webhook carve-out (`tasks.py:1120-1121`), which only happens if the agent or a human pushes again.

4. Trigger frequency: a GitHub incident, a product-DB failover, or Temporal being unreachable for longer than ~15 s at the moment the PR URL lands are all ordinary production events, so the loss is reachable, not hypothetical.

Caveat that lowers severity from must_fix: the claim that this leg is uniquely "without webhook redelivery" is wrong. `products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:63-64` ACKs GitHub with 202 before the Celery task runs, and `process_pull_request_event` (`tasks.py:809`) uses the identical `max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5` policy with the same "webhook is already ACKed, so retry" reasoning (`tasks.py:823-828`). So the inbox leg matches the product's existing durability bar; the gap is real but pre-existing in shape, blast radius is one missed initial draft review (a later push re-reviews), and a proportionate fix is a longer backoff (`retry_backoff=True`, higher `max_retries`) rather than a new reconciliation task.
votes.refutation: Tried to refute three ways. (a) Precedent: the webhook path uses the same 3x5s policy and GitHub does not redeliver after the 202 ACK, so the inbox leg is not worse than the existing design; this shows parity, not that the trigger is unreachable. (b) Refire: the receiver does re-fire on any output-touching save and the task's head-keyed dedupe correctly creates or restarts the run on refire (tasks.py:1197-1213), but no code path guarantees a later output save; the webhook backstop write is one-shot and the agent server writes output at its own discretion. (c) Reconciliation: searched for a beat/sweeper task that recreates missing or restarts stranded QUEUED inbox runs; only the daily digest is scheduled. All three refutations fail, so a >15 s transient outage at hand-off time does permanently lose the initial review unless something else pushes to the PR.
